test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 14 Oct, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The strength of Supreme Court has increased to how many judges as of May 2026?
solution:
The correct answer is __**37**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The strength of the Supreme Court of India has been increased to **37 judges** as of **May 2026.**
 
• The Union Cabinet chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today has approved the proposal for introducing The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026 in Parliament to amend The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956 for increasing the number of Judges of the Supreme Court of India by **4** from the present **33 **to **37 **(excluding the Chief Justice of India). 
 
• The increase in the number of judges aims to reduce the pendency of cases and expedite the delivery of justice.
 
• The last increase in the number of judges was approved by the President of India in August 2019, from 31 to 34.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Judicial Appointments**: Judges of the Supreme Court are appointed by the President of India under Article 124(2) of the Constitution.
 
• **Collegium System**: The appointment of judges follows the collegium system, where the Chief Justice of India and a forum of four senior-most judges recommend the appointments.
 
• **Retirement Age**: The retirement age for Supreme Court judges in India is 65 years.
 
• **Jurisdiction**: The Supreme Court has original, appellate, and advisory jurisdiction, making it the highest judicial authority in India.
